message.content:
**Rough estimate:** Painting the entire Eiffel Tower takes **about 2 years** of continuous work. --- ### Why 2 years? | Step | What’s involved | Typical duration | |------|-----------------|------------------| | **1. Preparation** (cleaning, rust removal, scaffolding setup) | • 18,000+ rivets are inspected and cleaned
• 5,000 t of iron is sprayed with a rust‑prevention primer
• 60 000 L of paint is stored on site | 6–9 months | | **2. Priming** | • Primer coats every exposed surface to stop corrosion | 3–4 months | | **3. Painting** | • Two layers of protective paint (usually a special “Eiffel Tower” enamel)
• Workers paint in shifts, covering ~1 m² per worker per day | 12–15 months | | **4. Final inspection & touch‑ups** | • Quality control, final sealant, removal of scaffolding | 1–2 months | > **Total:** ~24–30 months (≈ 2 years) --- ### Context * **Repainting cycle:** The tower is repainted every **7 years** to keep the iron protected. * **Workforce:** About **200–250 workers** (painters, technicians, safety staff) work in shifts. * **Safety & logistics:** The tower’s height (330 m) and the need for scaffolding and rope access mean that work is staged in sections, often with temporary platforms and safety nets. --- ### Bottom line If you’re asking how long it would take a crew to paint the Eiffel Tower from start to finish, the answer is roughly **two years** of continuous, phased work. If you’re asking how often the tower gets repainted, it’s about **every 7 years**.
